evidence.positive: Against the running instance (mayo-mayo tenant, which is the only tenant whose antibiotic-pathways.csv fills the new Acuity column) I created four p-cesarean-delivery cases via POST /api/admin/patients/ + /operations/create and set acuity with PATCH /operations/{caseId}/acuity, then read GET /api/admin/patients/{pmrn}/operations/{caseId}/antibiotic-candidates. ELECTIVE case 73672 returned outcome=RECOMMENDED caseAcuity=ELECTIVE recommended=[CEFAZOLIN], with pos=0 acuities=["ELECTIVE"] appliesToCase=true and pos=1 acuities=["URGENT","EMERGENT"] appliesToCase=false. URGENT case 81421 returned recommended=[CEFAZOLIN+AZITHROMYCIN] with the two appliesToCase flags exactly inverted. The boot log carries the import-time scope-coverage warning the ticket asks for: 'p-cesarean-delivery has no pathway for NON_URGENT, no acuity, so such a case resolves to no guidance'. DB shows antibiotic_pathway_acuities holding ELECTIVE for pathway 0 and URGENT+EMERGENT for pathway 1 in mayo-mayo only (demo-demo, mgb-mgh, mgb-icsnh hold 0 rows), and all three tenant CSVs carry the header 'Procedure,Risk,Acuity,Pathway'. Cache-drop deliverable exercised end to end over real HL7: an Epic SIU^S14 (PV1-4 Elec, AIS 'CESAREAN SECTION') posted to /api/admin/hl7-inbound-messages/send created case 990001 with acuity=ELECTIVE and p-cesarean-delivery attached; a medication scan (POST /api/cds/medication-selection/98765001/990001) populated valkey key 'antibiotic-resolution-v3/tenant:mayo-mayo/op:01a04a0d-6683-7259-8f5a-bfbae3381c89'; a second SIU carrying PV1-4 Urg and no AIS segments moved the row to URGENT and the key was gone from valkey afterwards, and re-reading the case then returned recommended=[CEFAZOLIN+AZITHROMYCIN].
evidence.negative: The elective case is never offered the labouring regimen: for case 73672 the azithromycin pathway reported appliesToCase=false and AZITHROMYCIN was absent from recommended in every read. A case carrying no acuity matched only pathways naming none: case 79896 (acuity null) returned outcome=NOT_CONFIGURED recommended=[] with both pathways appliesToCase=false, and the app logged 'Operation 01a04a0a-8347-7442-89f1-7dff9cb2a5aa matched no antibiotic pathway for p-cesarean-delivery: 2 configured, procedure risk LOW case acuity none'. NON_URGENT case 61486 behaved the same way ('... case acuity NON_URGENT'), matching the documented deferred gap. The inverse of 'blank acuity stops matching' was checked too, since that would break four cases in five: three p-adrenalectomy cases (unscoped row, blank Acuity) with acuity null, ELECTIVE and NON_URGENT all returned outcome=RECOMMENDED with appliesToCase=true. For the cache drop, the no-change case was checked: an SIU repeating PV1-4 Elec with no AIS segments left the acuity at ELECTIVE and left the valkey key 'antibiotic-resolution-v3/tenant:mayo-mayo/op:01a04a0d-...' in place.
evidence.red_check: Two data flips, both reverted. Flip 1: UPDATE mayo-mayo.antibiotic_pathway_acuities SET acuity='NON_URGENT' for pathway 01a04a05-9a87-78fc-8855-d9b8b46a65bf, so the cefazolin pathway no longer named ELECTIVE. Re-reading case 73672 went red immediately: outcome flipped RECOMMENDED -> NOT_CONFIGURED, recommended=[] , both pathways appliesToCase=false, and the app logged for the first and only time 'matched no antibiotic pathway for p-cesarean-delivery: 2 configured, procedure risk LOW case acuity ELECTIVE'. Reverted to ELECTIVE and case 73672 returned to RECOMMENDED / [CEFAZOLIN]. Flip 2, aimed at the ticket's actual absence assertion: INSERT ELECTIVE into the acuities of pathway 01a04a05-9a8c-73ee-b1be-e01be4e24463 (the azithromycin one). Case 73672 then returned recommended=[CEFAZOLIN, CEFAZOLIN+AZITHROMYCIN] with both pathways appliesToCase=true - the elective section being offered the labouring regimen, which is precisely what the ticket exists to prevent. Deleted that row again; final state is three acuity rows (pathway 0 ELECTIVE, pathway 1 EMERGENT+URGENT) and all four cases re-read green. The pre-fix class swap was deliberately not attempted: AntibioticPathway at 2b301ca38^ has neither the acuities collection nor appliesTo, while the shipped importer and ProcedureAntibioticCandidateService both call them, so the swapped class would fail to link at config import rather than mis-scope pathways - a boot failure, not the behaviour under test.

red_check_signature: matched no antibiotic pathway for p-cesarean-delivery: 2 configured, procedure risk LOW case acuity ELECTIVE
caveats: The debugger's React tab (one 'case acuity' badge plus the acuities badge on each pathway) was never rendered in a browser; its two data sources, caseAcuity and pathway.acuities/appliesToCase, were read directly off the API response instead.
Only mayo-mayo actually configures acuity today, so the scope predicate was exercised on p-cesarean-delivery alone; demo and MGB were confirmed to hold zero acuity rows rather than exercised.
The Mayo FHIR case-start and MGB surgical-record acuity writers were not exercised - only the Epic SIU scheduling feed and the admin acuity edit.
The addition of antibiotic_pathway_acuities to TenantResetService.PRESERVED_TABLES was not exercised; no tenant reset was run.

automation.assessment: Unit coverage of the scope predicate itself is already strong and does not need duplicating: AntibioticPathwayResolutionSpecTest has ten acuity cases (acuityScopedPathwayAppliesOnlyAtThatAcuity, unscopedPathwayAppliesAtEveryAcuity, caseWithoutAcuityMatchesOnlyUnscopedPathways, caseWithAnUnmappedAcuityMatchesOnlyUnscopedPathways, acuityAndRiskAreBothRequired and more), and AntibioticPathwayCSVImporterTest covers the column, the token vocabulary, the pipe separator, unrecognized acuities, the uncovered-scope warning and the bundled Mayo file. The real hole is the fifth deliverable. DefaultHL7ProcessingContextSchedulingFieldsTest only pins the static applySchedulingFields merge; nothing tests that saveOperation drops the cached resolution when a scheduling message changes the acuity, nor that it leaves the entry alone when the acuity is unchanged, and that branch is the one that silently regresses because the procedure-names branch masks it whenever AIS segments are present.
proposed_tests: DefaultHL7ProcessingContext.saveOperation with no procedure names and a changed acuity deletes the antibiotic-resolution cache key for the case, after commit rather than before
DefaultHL7ProcessingContext.saveOperation with no procedure names and an unchanged acuity leaves the cached resolution in place
DefaultHL7ProcessingContext.saveOperation on a brand-new case does not attempt a cache drop (storedCase null, prior acuity null)
End-to-end Mayo SIU test: an S14 changing PV1-4 from Elec to Urg on an existing cesarean case moves the resolution from CEFAZOLIN to CEFAZOLIN+AZITHROMYCIN

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: An elective Mayo cesarean case resolved to cefazolin alone while an urgent one resolved to cefazolin with azithromycin, from the same procedure's two acuity-scoped pathways.
Negative: A case carrying no acuity, and a non-urgent case, both matched no pathway and resolved NOT_CONFIGURED, while unscoped pathways for other procedures still matched cases at every acuity including none.
Red check: Retargeting the elective pathway's acuity in the database dropped the elective case to NOT_CONFIGURED and produced the no-match log line, and adding elective to the azithromycin pathway offered the elective case that regimen; both were reverted.

Automation: The scope predicate and the importer are already well covered by unit tests, but the cache drop on an acuity-changing scheduling message is not, and is proposed.
